questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Velocity depends on the frame that reports it
questions.learningObjective: state that the measured value of a velocity depends on the reference frame
questions.stem: A train runs at 30 m/s past a platform, and a passenger inside the train watches the platform slide past. Which pair of statements about the two measured speeds is correct?

options.text: Ground sees the train at 30 m/s forward and the train sees the platform at 30 m/s backward
Ground sees the train at 30 m/s forward and the train sees the platform as being permanently at rest
options.misconception: believes a body is at rest in every frame at once

options.text: Both observers must agree on 30 m/s since speed is a property the train carries with it
options.misconception: believes speed is a frame-independent property of an object

options.text: Only the ground frame can measure a speed, since the other frame is defined by the moving train
options.misconception: believes only the ground frame is a legitimate reference frame

questions.explanation: Velocity is a rate of change of position, and position means nothing until a frame supplies the coordinate grid, so one motion carries two perfectly good values. The ground frame sees the train moving at 30 m/s; the train frame sees the platform moving at 30 m/s in the opposite sense. Nothing conflicts, because the two sentences describe the same arrangement on two different grids, and a body is at rest in exactly one inertial frame, namely its own.
questions.hint: Ask which object each observer has chosen to treat as stationary.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: The assumption inside a Galilean velocity transformation
questions.learningObjective: identify the assumption that a Galilean transformation of velocity makes
questions.stem: A Galilean transformation adds the frame speed to a velocity and leaves time untouched. Which assumption must hold for that rule to be self-consistent?

options.text: Clocks in every inertial frame tick at the same rate, so all frames share one time
Rulers in every frame report identical lengths, so contraction can never be observed
options.misconception: believes length invariance is required for velocity addition

options.text: Light returns from a mirror at the same speed it left in every frame
options.misconception: treats frame-independent light speed as a Galilean premise

options.text: The speed of light is infinite, so all travel times vanish under a change of frame
options.misconception: believes a change of frame removes propagation delay

questions.explanation: Galilean velocity addition is nothing more than absolute time in disguise: if every clock keeps the same rate, the time interval in the numerator is shared, and subtracting one velocity from another follows. The rule is not bad arithmetic; it is arithmetic resting on an assumption that no experiment has granted. It is the assumption about time, not any claim about light or rulers, that the search for a moving frame forced us to abandon.
questions.hint: Velocity is distance divided by time, so ask which of the two is being held shared.

questions.topic: What a null fringe shift rules out
questions.learningObjective: interpret the null result of a rotating interferometer
questions.stem: An interferometer with perpendicular arms is turned slowly through a full revolution on a turntable and the fringe pattern never shifts. What has this measurement ruled out?

options.text: A difference in round-trip light time between the two arm directions, of the size the effect predicted
Any dependence of light on the direction the apparatus happens to point
options.misconception: reads a null result as proof of complete directional independence

options.text: The use of more than one path through the apparatus to compare two beams
options.misconception: concludes the whole two-path method is invalid

options.text: The presence of a material medium, since any medium would bend one arm
options.misconception: overstates the null result as ruling out all media

questions.explanation: The two arms were set at right angles precisely because a light-carrying medium would make the along-arm and across-arm round trips unequal, and rotating the apparatus would then change that difference and shift the fringes. A null result bounds an effect rather than measuring it, so the honest conclusion is a limit, not a zero.
questions.hint: Work out what the design would show if the predicted difference were real and large.

questions.topic: The postulate that removes a preferred frame
questions.learningObjective: state the first postulate of special relativity and the picture it replaces
questions.stem: Special relativity begins from a postulate about light. Which statement is that postulate, and what does it displace?

Each observer measures the light speed of the source he is moving with
options.misconception: confuses the postulate with frame dependence it removes

options.text: All signals travel at the same speed in every frame, with light singled out afterwards
options.misconception: extends the frame invariance to signals that are not lightlike

options.text: Light possesses a rest frame in which its speed is defined and maximal
options.misconception: believes light defines a preferred frame of its own

The postulate settles that no experiment can single out one frame by measuring light speed alone; the transformation law then has to be whatever leaves that speed unchanged.

questions.topic: Where the Lorentz factor goes as speed reaches light speed
questions.learningObjective: describe the limiting behaviour of the Lorentz factor
questions.stem: The Lorentz factor equals one over the square root of one minus the square of the speed as a fraction of light speed. How does it behave as that fraction approaches one?

options.text: It grows without bound, so no finite value of it corresponds to a massive body at light speed
It settles at one, since at that speed a body would simply be at rest with itself
options.misconception: believes the limit describes a photon resting in its own frame

options.text: It falls to zero, which is why a very fast body carries so little energy
options.misconception: confuses an unbounded factor with a vanishing energy

options.text: It is always one, because the factor depends on no velocity at all in any frame
options.misconception: believes the factor is one regardless of the relative speed

questions.explanation: As the speed fraction approaches one from below, the bracket approaches zero from above, and one over a vanishing number diverges instead of settling. That divergence is the working statement of the whole theory: massless particles sit at light speed, and massive ones only approach it, never arriving. In the rest frame of any body the speed fraction is zero and the factor is exactly one, a useful check that the quantity is always a comparison between two frames rather than a property of the body.
questions.hint: Look at the bracket in the denominator as the speed fraction climbs.

questions.learningObjective: state what two identical clocks show when reunited after a trip
questions.stem: Two identical clocks are synchronised while side by side, then one is carried at constant speed on a closed trip and the two are compared when they meet again. What does the pair of readings show?

options.text: The carried clock shows less elapsed time, so elapsed time is a path quantity in spacetime
Both clocks show identical elapsed time, since each experienced the same events
options.misconception: believes identical clocks keep identical readings on a closed trip

options.text: The carried clock shows more elapsed time, since its own motion added energy to it
options.misconception: believes motion speeds up a clock rather than slowing it

options.text: Only the carried clock can be judged, since the stationary one was never compared
options.misconception: dismisses the comparison of the two readings as untestable

Because the arrangement is symmetric before the trip and not after it, the comparison can only be made once, at the reunion, and that is where the asymmetry shows.

questions.learningObjective: identify which component of an object's length is reduced and in which sense

A length longer than 2.0 m, since motion stretches an object along its own axis

questions.topic: Where the asymmetry in a twin journey sits
questions.learningObjective: explain the resolution of the travelling twin age difference
questions.stem: One twin makes a constant-speed round trip in a spaceship while the other stays at home, and on reunion the traveller is younger. Which feature of the journey accounts for the difference?

options.text: The traveller changes inertial frames on the way out and back, and the change of frame holds the asymmetry
The brief acceleration at turnaround subtracts age in proportion to how hard the turn was
options.misconception: believes accumulated acceleration produces the age difference

options.text: The home twin's clock runs slow throughout because it sits inside a gravitational field
options.misconception: borrows gravitational slowing to explain a purely inertial trip

options.text: The traveller's clock runs slow in every frame, so the gap is just the Lorentz factor
options.misconception: believes one clock is slow with no frame change required

The home twin never leaves a single frame, so no such step ever happens on that clock, and acceleration merely marks the handover.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Relativistic momentum against velocity
questions.learningObjective: describe how relativistic momentum grows with speed
questions.stem: The momentum of a particle is written as the Lorentz factor times its rest mass times its velocity. How does that momentum respond as the speed climbs toward light speed?

options.text: It grows faster than the velocity does, so no finite push brings a massive body to light speed
It grows in strict proportion to the velocity, which is the classical rule carried upward
options.misconception: believes the momentum keeps its classical linear form

options.text: It falls toward zero, so a very fast particle is harder to stop than a slow one
options.misconception: believes fast particles carry less momentum than slow ones

options.text: It settles at a fixed value, because only the mass can still grow with speed
options.misconception: believes the mass term alone carries the whole effect

questions.explanation: The extra factor is itself unbounded as the speed nears light speed, so the momentum runs away faster than the velocity, and it is that runaway rather than any special prohibition that keeps a massive body short of the ceiling. A particle given a thousand times the energy at the same rest mass is not a thousand times faster, since the speed has only a narrow band left to move in. Momentum itself is an ordinary vector whose components any frame agrees on, so the change is in its connection to a velocity measured alongside it.
questions.hint: Consider what the extra factor does to the ratio of momentum to velocity.

questions.topic: The classical limit of the total energy
questions.learningObjective: recover the classical kinetic energy from the relativistic total energy
questions.stem: The total energy of a particle is the Lorentz factor times its rest mass times light speed squared. How does that expression behave when the speed becomes small?

options.text: The factor approaches one, so the expression reduces to rest energy plus a classical kinetic term
The factor grows without limit, so the classical kinetic term becomes the dominant correction
options.misconception: believes the factor diverges at low rather than high speed

options.text: The factor approaches zero, so the total energy collapses to the kinetic term alone
options.misconception: believes the rest energy disappears in the classical limit

options.text: The rest term vanishes, leaving exactly the familiar kinetic energy of one half mv squared
options.misconception: believes rest energy and classical kinetic energy exclude each other

questions.explanation: Expanding the factor for a small speed fraction gives one plus half the square of that fraction, and multiplying through by the rest energy reproduces one half of mass times velocity squared to lowest order, so the classical result is the low-speed shadow of the relativistic one. The rest energy is the piece left when the speed goes to zero, and keeping it is what lets the same expression describe a stationary body and a particle of light. A theory that forgot the rest term would still work in motion and would fail the moment anything stopped.
questions.hint: Expand the square root for a small fraction and read off the leading correction.

questions.topic: What converting a mass into energy releases
questions.learningObjective: apply the mass-energy relation to a stated mass
questions.stem: A stationary mass of 1.0 g is converted entirely into radiation. What does the mass-energy relation say about the energy that appears?

About 9.0e10 J of radiation, because one gram of mass is worth that much energy
options.misconception: loses three factors of ten by mishandling the speed of light

options.text: About 1.8e20 J of radiation, because the released energy scales with the mass squared
options.misconception: treats the conversion as quadratic in the mass rather than linear

options.text: No energy at all, because the mass is gone and the mass carried it away
options.misconception: believes a change of form cancels the energy the mass held

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: The combination of energy and momentum that all frames share
questions.learningObjective: identify the frame-invariant combination of energy and momentum
questions.stem: A free particle carries a total energy E and a momentum of magnitude p, and its rest mass m is fixed. Which combination of E and p must be identical in every frame?

options.text: E squared minus p squared c squared, which reduces to the rest mass squared times c to the fourth
E divided by p, which must come out as the speed of light in every frame
options.misconception: believes the ratio of energy to momentum is frame invariant

options.text: E plus p c, which is the rest energy and the kinetic energy simply added together
options.misconception: believes the sum of energy and momentum is the invariant

options.text: p divided by E, which is the inverse speed and so never changes between frames
options.misconception: believes the inverse speed ratio is the quantity that is conserved

questions.explanation: The transformation mixes energy and momentum linearly, and the one combination it leaves untouched is the difference of their squares, which in the particle's own frame is just the rest mass term. Every frame describing that same particle therefore agrees on this number while disagreeing separately about the energy and the momentum. This is the invariant that a balanced reaction must preserve on both sides, and it is the quickest way to reject a proposed process whose energy and momentum cannot both be conserved.
questions.hint: Try the combination on the particle viewed in its own rest frame.

questions.topic: Threshold for creating a particle pair
questions.learningObjective: state why a pair of particles sets an energy threshold
questions.stem: A high-energy photon strikes a nucleus and produces an electron and a positron. What sets the smallest photon energy that can bring this about?

One rest energy of one, because a positron is an electron and the pair shares a single mass
options.misconception: counts a single rest energy for a pair of separate particles

options.text: No energy at all, because the nucleus supplies the whole cost and the photon adds nothing
options.misconception: believes the nucleus pays the entire energy of the pair

options.text: Four rest energies, because each particle must carry a doubled rest energy to be real
options.misconception: doubles the rest energy of each particle a second time

Equal and opposite momenta guarantee only that the total momentum is zero, which is a conservation statement and not a check on whether the individual energies are possible. The invariant is the test that separates a merely momentum-balanced set from a real one.
questions.hint: Check each particle against the invariant before trusting the conservation statement.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Why a transverse ruler is not contracted
questions.learningObjective: explain why the length change acts along the motion only
questions.stem: A rod passes an observer at relativistic speed and is measured to be shorter along its length of motion but unchanged across it. Explain in your own words why only one direction is affected.

answer.exemplar: The change comes from the mixing of space and time in the transform between the two frames, and that mixing only involves the direction along which the frames slide past one another. A ruler lying across the motion is never compared at two different times, because the two events chosen to fix its two ends happen at the same moment in the rod's own frame and are not the same pair of events in the ground frame, so no factor is generated for that direction. The rod's occupants therefore find both its length and its width unchanged, and the observer moving past finds the length shortened and the width untouched. This is not a squeezing of the object: nothing is compressed, and the difference lies entirely in which two events each observer uses to say where the ends are. It is also why a fast rod does not look like a thin plate, since a photograph records light from many emission times at once.

questions.explanation: The transform mixes the time and space coordinates only along the axis of relative motion, so the reduction is a property of that one direction and appears wherever two events are compared across different frames.
questions.hint: Ask which pairs of events each observer uses to locate the two ends of the rod.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Aberration and beaming from one transformation
questions.learningObjective: explain how one transform produces both a direction shift and a concentration of emission
questions.stem: Explain in your own words how a single change of frame accounts both for the light arriving from a shifted direction and for the faint cone of light seen ahead of a fast source.

answer.exemplar: The transform acts on directions as well as on speeds and times, so light that left the source in some direction is seen by a moving observer to arrive from a different direction, tipped forward toward the direction the observer is travelling. That tip is aberration, and it is the same fact of frame equivalence that says no observer measures the light speed differently. The companion effect comes from asking the converse question: given a cone of observers spread out around the source, the transform maps them into a bundle that is far more tightly packed near the direction of travel than away from it, so a much larger share of them see the light. Forward of the source the angular spacing of observers is compressed, so the radiation is concentrated, and behind the source it is spread out, so that direction looks dim. A fast source therefore appears much brighter ahead than behind, and both halves of that statement come from the same tilt of the cone rather than from any extra assumption.

questions.explanation: Directions transform with the same law that fixes the speed of light, and the inverse map bunches observers together ahead of a moving source, so the shift and the concentration are two readings of one geometric fact.
questions.hint: Consider the inverse of the same transformation applied to a cone of observers.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Mirror images of a weak decay
questions.learningObjective: explain what a parity-violating decay says about a force
questions.stem: In one weak decay the products emerge preferentially in a direction related to the spin of the parent, and a mirror image of the experiment is never observed. Explain what this tells us about the interaction.

answer.exemplar: Parity is the operation of reflecting space, and if a law of physics is unchanged by that reflection then every experiment must have a mirror partner that behaves the same way. Observing decays that favour one handed arrangement, with the opposite handedness never appearing, means the weak interaction is not unchanged by the reflection, so it is a genuinely chiral interaction that treats the two mirror arrangements differently. Nothing is observed to be missing or depleted; the statement is about the propensity, and the overwhelming majority of candidates that would have restored parity symmetry were ruled out by experiment. The interesting consequence is not that the decay is unpredictable but that handedness becomes a measurable physical label, as real in an otherwise ordinary angular correlation, and that the same handedness shows up in more than one decay channel. Any deeper law that reproduces this must itself carry a handed structure, since a law with no preferred handedness could not produce a result that depends on it.

questions.explanation: A law unchanged by spatial reflection would produce mirror-equivalent decays, so a persistent preference in one handedness shows the weak interaction itself is not reflection symmetric, which makes handedness a measurable property.
questions.hint: Ask what a reflection-symmetric law would predict for the mirror of the experiment.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: What a change of character between neutrino states implies
questions.learningObjective: explain what the observation of neutrino oscillation implies about mass
questions.stem: A beam of neutrinos is found to arrive partway through its flight as a different kind of neutrino, at a rate that depends on distance and energy. Explain what this requires of the neutrino.

answer.exemplar: A particle whose type is a fixed label cannot change into another kind, so observing a change at all means the type is not an immutable property of the particle but a description of a state that evolves. The evolution is a superposition of states with slightly different rest energies, and since a state built from two rest energies is not itself a state of definite energy, the two components pick up different phases along the way and the mixture oscillates. The oscillation only has a rate if the two states differ in rest energy, so the two states cannot have equal masses, and the measurement of the energy dependence of the rate is a measurement of that difference. The key implication is that neutrinos, long treated as having no rest mass, must carry a small one, and its size is set by fitting the observed rates. Because the effect needs a baseline comparable with the oscillation length, which is long and inversely related to the energy, the phenomenon became visible only once detectors were built across such distances.

questions.explanation: Only a particle with more than one possible rest energy can be in a superposition that later resolves into different kinds, so a measured rate of change requires a mass difference and a small but nonzero neutrino rest mass.
questions.hint: Ask what a particle must possess before two different outcomes can arise from one initial state.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: A relativistic claim that the invariant forbids
questions.learningObjective: explain why a proposed observation conflicts with the invariant
questions.stem: A report claims a particle was seen with a total energy of 1.00 MeV and a momentum of 0.95 MeV per unit of light speed, with a rest energy of 0.30 MeV. Explain why that claim cannot stand.

answer.exemplar: The energy-momentum relation fixes the rest energy of a particle once its total energy and momentum are given, because the invariant says the square of the total energy equals the square of the momentum term plus the square of the rest energy. Inserting the reported numbers, the momentum term contributes 0.9025 in units of MeV squared and the stated rest energy contributes 0.09, giving 0.9925 against a total energy squared of 1.00, a discrepancy far larger than any measurement uncertainty in such a claim. Solving the same relation for the rest energy instead gives about 0.31 MeV from the total energy alone or about 0.312 MeV from the momentum alone, and those are the only values compatible, which is why the three quoted numbers cannot all be right. The point is that the invariant is a frame-independent consistency condition rather than a fitted relation, so a disagreement is not a matter of choosing a better constant or a different model of the motion. The plausible causes are a misread momentum, a misassigned particle, or a calibration error somewhere in the chain from track to energy, and each would have to be found by measuring the track curvature and the energy independently.

questions.explanation: The invariant fixes the rest energy from the total energy and momentum, and the three quoted values fail that check, so at least one measurement in the chain is wrong rather than the relation being approximate.
questions.hint: Substitute the reported numbers into the invariant and compare the two sides.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Why the classical rules had to be replaced rather than patched
questions.learningObjective: explain the logical steps from a null measurement to new transformation rules
questions.stem: Explain in your own words why a null measurement of light's speed through a proposed medium could not be absorbed by adjusting the classical rules, and what had to give instead.

answer.exemplar: The classical rules add velocities and take time to be the same for everyone, and together they make the speed of a signal depend on the motion of the source and the observer. That consequence had been measured and confirmed with sound and with light through moving media, so the two principles looked as secure as anything in mechanics. The rotating interferometer was built to test that consequence for light in empty space, and it returned nothing, which no adjustment of a classical parameter can produce, because every classical parameter still leaves a frame-dependence somewhere. The response was therefore to keep the principle that physics is the same in every inertial frame and to give up the assumption that time is absolute, replacing the additive velocity rule with one that mixes time into the transformation. The old rules survive as the slow-speed limit, exactly as they must, so nothing classical was thrown away, only its claim to hold exactly.

questions.explanation: The null result contradicts a prediction that follows from absolute time, so the assumption has to go and the transform with it, leaving the classical rules intact only as a limiting case.
questions.hint: Ask whether any choice of classical parameters can make a frame-dependent prediction disappear.

questions.topic: From a null measurement to a usable transform
questions.learningObjective: order the reasoning that turns a null result into relativistic mechanics

The prediction that a light-carrying medium would give a rotating fringe shift is tested and not found
Dilation and contraction of clocks and lengths are read off the transform as consequences
The measurement removes the preferred frame, so the principle of frame equivalence is kept without a medium

questions.explanation: The measurement has to come first, because it is the observation that forces the reasoning. Its null result removes the preferred frame, so the principle of frame equivalence is kept and the medium is dropped rather than the principle. The transform is then constrained by the requirement that every frame measure the same light speed, and that single requirement fixes both the factor and the way time mixes into it. Dilation of clocks and contraction of lengths are consequences read off afterwards, which is why they are predictions of the transform and not separate postulates.
questions.hint: Start from the observation, then the principle, then the rule, then its consequences.
